title: Orchestra V instrument definition
description: Data contract between the Orchestra V catalogue and the SFZ region compiler. One entry describes how a catalogue instrument is built out of the sample packs of one library.

id.description: Stable definition id stored on the track.

library.description: Which library in audio/orchestra-v/libraries.js holds this instrument's samples.

mirrors.description: The Orchestra Sampler catalogue id this instrument stands in for.

available.description: False when the library ships no samples for this instrument; the grid shows it greyed out.

sourcePack.description: Manifest pack name within the library, e.g. "violin" or "Tutti Strings".

pedal.description: True when a held sustain pedal (CC64) should keep released notes sounding, as on a piano.

percFolder.description: Restrict a pitched instrument to one sub-folder of its pack.

keymap.description: Percussion layout. Each entry pins one sample folder to one MIDI key.

keyRange.description: Advisory playable range [lo, hi]; the compiler still clamps to what the samples cover.

articulations.description: Ordered preference list. The first entry is the default technique.

velocityLayers.description: How dynamic layers are turned into velocity zones.

crossfadeWidth.description: Half-width in MIDI velocity units of the equal-power fade across a layer boundary.

voiceModel.description: Per-instrument voicing, carried over from the M Orchestra library metadata.

gainTrim.description: Output trim. Defaults to 0.55 because a synthesised section sums several detuned copies of one recording; a library that already recorded the ensemble sets it near unity.

velocityTrack.description: Share of the level that velocity controls, 0.45 by default. Instruments recorded at a single dynamic need more, because nothing else varies with how hard the key is struck.
